pages.text: Angie is an anglerfish living deep in the ocean. Down there, it is very dark because sunlight cannot reach.
The deep ocean is cold and quiet. Angie moves slowly, and tiny creatures float past like little dots.
Angie has a tiny light in front of her head. Some deep-sea animals make their own light called bioluminescence.
Angie wiggles her light like a small lantern. Curious little fish may come closer to see what it is.
Because it is so dark, light can help animals find food. Angie’s light is one smart deep-sea tool.
Not all ocean animals need a light. Animals change and adapt to the places where they live.
Angie waits patiently. In the deep sea, food can be harder to find, so waiting can help.
Far above, the surface ocean is bright. Down here, Angie lives in darkness, using her special light.
Angie reminds us: deep ocean is dark and cold, sunlight fades away, and some animals make light to help survive.
At bedtime, we whisper: the ocean has layers. Some are sunny, and some are deep, dark, and full of surprises.
